title: The universal call to holiness (Lumen Gentium 5)
hook: everyone is called to holiness, not only priests and religious

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sacrosanctum Concilium: nobody only watching at Mass. Your line was all of us, taking part. Today the council says the same about the rest of the week.

A night-shift nurse charts vitals at three in the morning. A father scrapes a burnt pan while a toddler narrates the whole thing. A bus driver waits, again, for someone running. It's easy to file holiness under somebody else's job, priests, monks and nuns, with everyone else doing their best from the cheap seats. The council's constitution on the Church gave a whole chapter to saying otherwise. Today: the universal call to holiness.
screen: `THREE IN THE MORNING.` → `THE CHEAP SEATS.` → `THE UNIVERSAL CALL TO HOLINESS.`

segments.voice: The constitution is called Lumen Gentium, light of the nations, and its fifth chapter carries a plain title: the universal call to holiness in the Church. It starts with Jesus, who preached holiness to every one of his disciples, of whatever condition. The council quotes him, and in the Douay-Rheims the line reads: "Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect." He didn't say it to a select few. Then it draws the conclusion plainly: all the faithful, whatever their rank or state of life, are called to the fullness of Christian life and the perfection of love. Not a smaller holiness for laypeople and a bigger one for clergy. One holiness. Saint Paul had put it in a phrase: "For this is the will of God, your sanctification." Then the part that lands on a Tuesday: that one holiness is lived in many different kinds of life. The council names married couples and parents, people who work hard with their hands, the poor, the sick and those who suffer. Holiness grows, it says, in the very conditions and duties of each one's life, done with faith. A different chapter of the same document pictures laypeople making the world holy from the inside, like leaven in dough. So the nurse, the father and the driver aren't waiting for holiness to arrive somewhere else. The council points to the shift they're already working.
screen: `JESUS SPOKE TO ALL HIS DISCIPLES.` · `ONE HOLINESS, NOT TWO.` · `IN EACH ONE'S OWN DUTIES.` · `LEAVEN FROM THE INSIDE.` · then, large: `EVERYONE IS CALLED.`

segments.voice: Name your roles, one per breath: parent, friend, coworker, neighbor, student, patient, whatever fits, and then choose one. Ask what that role would look like with a bit more love and a bit more care, not something extra on top, just that role, done well. If you pray, offer it to God before the day takes over.
Lumen Gentium. Vatican Two's constitution on the Church, whose fifth chapter calls every member, in every state of life, to the fullness of love. Today's word.
Your line: everyone is called. Even a dull task done for someone else is on the map of holiness. Day seven hundred ninety-two.

howItsDone: Catholic teaching since Vatican II stresses that laypeople are called to holiness in their families and work, and some Catholics offer their day to God in a morning offering and look to lay saints as examples.
